## Overview
[The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict cross-border regional data isolation while maintaining compliance with GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US): Utilize video care, e-prescriptions, and the AI symptom checker.
- Licensed Clinicians: Conduct secure cross-border video consultations.
- Local Pharmacies: Receive national-standard e-prescriptions.
- Compliance / Regulatory Officers & External Regulatory Auditors: Access audit logs for accountability.
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform: GCP-hosted system (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`).
- Third-Party AI Model Provider: External service for symptom checking via HTTPS/REST.
- National E-Prescription Gateways / Pharmacy Networks: External systems using mTLS APIs.

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians to Platform: HTTPS / WebRTC (supporting degraded modes down to 300 kbit/s).
- Platform to Third-Party AI Model Provider: HTTPS/REST with payload pseudonymization.
- Platform to E-Prescription Gateways: mTLS APIs using HL7 FHIR and national standards.
- Inter-Region Link (EU to US): Zero-Trust link permitted only with cryptographically signed Patient Consent Tokens.
- Auditors to Platform: Secure, read-only HTTPS/SFTP export for audit logs.

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce regional data residency.
- Encryption: AES-256 with CMEK for data-at-rest; TLS 1.3 for data-in-transit.
- Authentication & Authorization: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with MFA and RBAC at the API gateway.
- Interoperability: HL7 FHIR (US) and national e-prescription standards (EU).

## Rationale
[This architecture ensures stringent regional compliance by separating data storage between GCP regions while maintaining secure, consent-driven cross-border access. It guarantees high availability and traceability to satisfy international healthcare regulations.]

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency while ensuring HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patients (EU/US), Licensed Clinicians, Local Pharmacies, Regulators, System Administrators, and Caregivers/Guardians.
- **Client Applications**: Flutter/React Native Web and Mobile Apps.
- **Backend Containers**: Kong API Gateway/BFF, Spring Boot Core Telehealth Service, FastAPI AI Symptom Checker, Node.js E-Prescription Service, Java Consent Management Service, and Node.js/Go Billing & Localization Container.
- **Data & Infrastructure**: GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL), GCP Cloud Storage, GCP Cloud Pub/Sub, and Cloud KMS.

## Relationships
- **Clients to API Gateway**: HTTPS and WebSockets using TLS 1.3 and OAuth2/OIDC authentication.
- **Internal Containers**: gRPC and GCP Cloud Pub/Sub protected by mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh.
- **External Integration**: National E-Prescription Gateways and Pharmacy Networks via HL7 FHIR and national standards.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider**: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce regional data isolation.
- **Backend & API**: Spring Boot, FastAPI, Node.js, and Kong API Gateway for scalable microservices.
- **Security**: Cloud KMS with CMEK, VPC Service Controls, and signed PASETO/JWT tokens for consent enforcement.
- **Messaging**: GCP Cloud Pub/Sub with client-side payload encryption for cross-service events.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates health data within regional boundaries using GCP regions, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA constraints. Dedicated microservices for consent and billing ensure regulatory compliance, security, and traceability under the EU MDR.

The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and EU MDR traceability while supporting low-bandwidth rural environments.

- FastAPI AI Symptom Checker

- WebRTC Media Client -> Kong API Gateway: Adaptive video streaming via ICE/TURN over UDP with TCP/TLS fallback and SRTP/DTLS-SRTP
- Regional Services -> GCP Cloud SQL: Data storage isolated within `europe-west3` (EU) and `us-central1` (US)

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend Framework:** Flutter / React Native for cross-platform web and mobile deployment
- **Local Storage & Security:** SQLCipher (AES-256) backed by Android Keystore and iOS Keychain for secure offline caching
- **Communication Protocols:** HTTPS, WebSockets (TLS 1.3), WebRTC, SRTP, and DTLS-SRTP for secure low-bitrate video
- **Backend Frameworks:** Spring Boot (Java), FastAPI (Python), and Node.js for microservices
- **Cloud Infrastructure:** Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict multi-region compliance (GDPR/HIPAA) by isolating data processing and storage within designated GCP regions. Client-side security controls, offline caching, and WebRTC fallback mechanisms guarantee reliable, secure telehealth delivery even for rural users with unstable connections.

## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture enforces strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for unstable rural connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US), Licensed Clinicians, Local Pharmacies, Compliance Officers
- Kong API Gateway/BFF (with Geo-Routing, JWT/OIDC Interceptor, Payload Compression, Header Enrichment)
- Spring Boot Core Telehealth Service
- FastAPI AI Symptom Checker
- Node.js E-Prescription Service
- Java Consent Management Service
- Node.js/Go Billing & Localization Container
- GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL), GCP Cloud Storage, GCP Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloud KMS
- GCP Regions: `europe-west3`, `us-central1`

## Relationships
- Flutter/React Native Web and Mobile Apps -> Kong API Gateway/BFF: Sends API requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3 / WebSockets with OAuth2/OIDC and DPoP]
- Kong API Gateway/BFF -> Spring Boot Core Telehealth Service: Routes core telehealth requests [gRPC / mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh]
- Kong API Gateway/BFF -> FastAPI AI Symptom Checker: Routes symptom check requests [gRPC / mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh]
- Kong API Gateway/BFF -> Node.js E-Prescription Service: Routes e-prescription requests [gRPC / mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh]
- Kong API Gateway/BFF -> Java Consent Management Service: Validates consent and tokens [gRPC / mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh]
- Kong API Gateway/BFF -> Node.js/Go Billing & Localization Container: Forwards localized requests [gRPC / mTLS via Anthos Service Mesh]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud infrastructure spanning `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for data residency.
- Kong API Gateway: Acts as BFF, enforcing geo-routing, rate limiting, and header injection via custom plugins.
- Spring Boot (Java) & FastAPI (Python): Core telehealth services and AI symptom checker container implementation.
- Node.js & Go: E-prescription, billing, and localization container runtimes.
